name: Apollo 11 (Tranquility Base)
description: The first crewed Moon landing, in Mare Tranquillitatis in July 1969.
why_interesting: A flat, near-equator site where the Sun rises and sets every ~29.5 days and Earth stays high in the sky. A good baseline for comparing polar sites.

name: Apollo 15 (Hadley-Apennine)
description: Landed between the Apennine Mountains and Hadley Rille, and was the first mission to drive a lunar rover.
why_interesting: Mountains nearby make it a mid-latitude site where real terrain could change sunrise and sunset times.

name: Apollo 17 (Taurus-Littrow)
description: The last crewed Moon landing, in the Taurus-Littrow valley in December 1972.
why_interesting: A valley floor surrounded by massifs, so the local horizon is higher than at a flat mare site.

name: Blue Ghost Mission 1 (Mare Crisium)
description: A commercial CLPS lander that touched down upright in Mare Crisium in March 2025.
why_interesting: It worked through a full lunar day and recorded the sunset, a clean example of a day-length mission at low latitude.

name: SLIM (Shioli crater)
description: Japan's precision lander, which landed within about 100 m of its target in January 2024 but ended up tipped on its nose.
why_interesting: Its solar panels faced the wrong way, so it only got power once the Sun moved across the sky. Panel orientation matters as much as sunlight.

name: Reiner Gamma
description: A bright swirl on Oceanus Procellarum linked to a local magnetic field.
why_interesting: A planned CLPS target, near the western limb where Earth sits lower in the sky than at the Apollo sites.

name: Chang'e 4 (Von Karman crater)
description: The first soft landing on the Moon's far side, inside Von Karman crater in January 2019.
why_interesting: Earth is never visible from here, so direct-to-Earth comms are impossible and it needed the Queqiao relay satellite.

name: Chandrayaan-3 (Shiv Shakti Point)
description: India's first soft landing, at high southern latitude in August 2023.
why_interesting: The Sun stays low in the sky here, so shadows are long and solar power is weaker than near the equator.

name: IM-1 Odysseus (near Malapert A)
description: The first commercial Moon landing, near Malapert A crater in February 2024. The lander tipped onto its side.
why_interesting: Near the south pole the Sun skims the horizon, so a tilted lander and nearby hills can cut power a lot.

name: IM-2 Athena (Mons Mouton)
description: Landed on the Mons Mouton plateau in March 2025 but came to rest on its side in a cold, shadowed crater.
why_interesting: With too little sunlight on its panels it ran out of power within about a day, showing how unforgiving south pole lighting is.

name: Shackleton Connecting Ridge
description: A raised ridge running from the rim of Shackleton crater, right next to the south pole.
why_interesting: High ground near the pole gets sunlight for most of the year and sits next to permanently shadowed craters that may hold ice.
